thread.title_full: City of Robbinsdale to pay $1.175 million settlement - NewsBreak

author: Anja Wuolu
title: City of Robbinsdale to pay $1.175 million settlement - NewsBreak
text:
By Anja Wuolu ,
16 hours ago
About five years ago, area police officers responded to a Robbinsdale man who was drunk, suicidal and holding a gun. During the incident, the man was shot.
Adam Nelson, a Robbinsdale resident in 2020, was shot with nine bullets by Crystal Police Officer Geoffrey Kusick, who was assisting the Robbinsdale Police Department at the time. Nelson survived the shooting, but according to the lawsuit, he was left with debilitating injuries that prevent him from working.
The incident was investigated by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and no charges were filed against Kusick by the Hennepin County Attorney. But, earlier this year, Nelson filed a civil lawsuit asking for $20 million.
"Recently, a tentative settlement was reached," City Manager Tim Sandvik said during a council meeting. "The settlement includes payment to Mr. Nelson and the amount of $3.175 million. Of this amount, $2 million will be paid by the League of Minnesota Cities' insurance trust, and the remaining will be contributed by the city of Robbinsdale. The settlement resolves all the civil litigation stemming from the July 12, 2020 incident.
"The agreement allows the parties to avoid Protractor litigation, which may have taken several years to resolve. The settlement does not assume fault by any of the named parties in the city supports actions of all officers on scene as necessary and justified to protect public safety."
Though discussion was mostly held in a closed session, the Robbinsdale City Council voted to accept this tentative settlement publicly on Oct. 7.
According to Vicki Hruby, the attorney representing the city, "The City of Robbinsdale is involved in this civil action as it requested Crystal officers, including Sgt. Geoffrey Kusick, to provide mutual aid during a welfare check on July 11, 2020. As the City requested this assistance, the City of Robbinsdale is the municipality involved in this lawsuit."
City Council Member Aaron Wagner commented briefly on the settlement, noting that it was difficult and they took it seriously.
"I think we worked together in a very real way to come up with a solution that was responsible," he said at the dais.
